blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (E-mail address and display name written to application logs) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: log.info("new signup email=%s name=%s id=%s", email, display_name, user_id)
findings.recommendation: Log only the opaque id (`log.info("new signup id=%s", user_id)`). As written, every sign-up copies the member's e-mail address and display name into the application logs, which have their own retention and access and are not reached by account erasure (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 32).
findings.title: E-mail address and display name written to application logs

findings.recommendation: Drop `email` from the event properties: the stated purpose ("Sign-ups are counted in product analytics") needs no e-mail address, and `user_id` already identifies the event. As written, each sign-up ships the member's e-mail address to the third-party processor at beacon.example.com, where account erasure does not reach it (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25, Art. 28). Also identify Beacon as a processor in the plan and state whether it transfers data outside the EEA (Chapter V).
findings.title: E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS

findings.evidence: - [x] personal-data — collects e-mail addresses and display names
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: state the purpose and lawful basis for collecting the e-mail address and display name, their retention period (backups included), and how erasure and access reach the member row and the copies this change creates (logs, Beacon events). Only the controller can decide this; the proposal is silent (GDPR Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 6, Art. 15–20).
findings.title: No retention, erasure or lawful basis stated for the collected member data
